transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-25 10:00 PT, Duration: ~58 mins. Recorded by Fireflies. Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Elior (Redwood CSM); Ravi, Sofia, Kenji, Marta (HyperEdge).

Summary: quick partner motion kickoff to align co-sell targets, review pipeline candidates, agree on escalation and who owns which outreach sequences. Agreed to draft one-pager + tech appendix and to prioritize three pilot logos.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — audio okay?
00:07 Ravi: Yep, can hear you. Thanks for setting up.
00:10 Maya: Cool. Really quick agenda — align on the list of accounts you want us to co-sell into, the handoff model, and any technical blockers for joint demos. Liam will cover the checklist and demo readiness.
00:25 Sofia: Sounds good. From our side we have a handful of strategic accounts where the co-sell could accelerate deals into Q1. We'll share a prioritized list.
00:33 Liam: Hi all, I'm Liam — SE on the partnership. I wanted to flag typical infra asks up front: VPC peering, private deploys, and latency expectations, especially for east-coast customers — we often recommend Redwood Dedicated or the private VPC path for that.
00:52 Kenji: Quick question on that — our security team always asks about KMS and audit logs. Is that part of the standard package?
00:58 Maya: Yes, we have KMS integrations and audit logs; we'll share the SOC2/ISO checklist. For private, we do offer customer-managed KMS options.
01:10 Ravi: Great. On the sales motion, we want to make sure the commission splits and who introduces whom is clear. We prefer to own the initial outreach and bring Redwood into an intro call once there's technical interest.
01:24 Maya: Totally reasonable — typical pattern is HyperEdge owns lead gen and discovery, Redwood joins for deeper technical touch and proofs. For larger deals we can coordinate an exec intro.
01:33 Marta: Any notes on pricing ranges? We need to know what band to present to customers.
01:38 Maya: We'll put together a simple banded pricing for co-sell proposals — not the final contract language but enough to position in first meetings.
01:45 Sofia: Also, what are your typical uptake rates for dedicated capacity — is there a minimum commit?
01:52 Liam: Dedicated has a baseline commit; we can show examples from similar customers. There's also burst policies for spiky usage. We'll send a sample committed plan.
02:04 Kenji: For demos, do you have a pre-built benchmark or is it all custom? We don't want to reinvent load tests.
02:11 Liam: We have a benchmark harness and a demo checklist — but depending on the model and sequence lengths you might need to tune KV cache and batching. Sometimes the -- sorry, the transcriber has me as 'KeyV cash' in the notes — but yeah, KV cache tuning is important.
02:27 Ravi: Ha, 'KeyV cash' — noted.
02:30 Maya: One thing to call out — co-sell success often hinges on escalation paths. If there's a contract/PO/legal hold, who do we escalate to? We propose a three-tier: AE/Partner rep -> Partnerships lead -> Customer exec sponsor.
02:46 Sofia: That works. Can Redwood commit to a 48-hour response SLA for partner escalations during active deal windows?
02:53 Elior: We can commit to that for priority deals; for enterprise we usually have a support SLA that can be bumped for co-sell pilots. We'll surface options.
03:04 Kenji: Technical blocker — some of our customers require air-gapped or on-prem inference for regulated data. Can Redwood run on-prem?
03:12 Liam: Yes, Redwood Private supports on-prem packages and VPC control-plane options. There's an onboarding lead time; we'll include rough timelines in the tech appendix.
03:23 Ravi: Great. Let's talk pipeline — we sent a spreadsheet earlier, but high-level, we have five logos we want to prioritize. Can we run a quick triage?
03:32 Maya: Sure — can you call them out and we'll score them for fit / closability / technical risk?
03:38 Sofia: First: AstraFin — strong fit, needs on-prem for some models. Second: NovaRetail — smaller, high chance Q1 close. Third: BlueMed — big logo, long procurement, needs dedicated capacity. Fourth: Cloudward — already talking to Anthropic — medium risk. Fifth: TerraOps — earliest pilot interest.
04:05 Liam: Quick reactions: AstraFin -> needs on-prem plus encryption at rest; BlueMed -> likely requires dedicated plus enhanced SLA; Cloudward -> competitor risk (Anthropic) so we should plan a differentiated technical narrative (e.g., latency/cost comparisons).
04:23 Maya: We'll score them 1-5 across technical risk and short-term close probability.
04:28 Ravi: Can you share the scoring rubric after?
04:30 Maya: Yes, I'll send the rubric and a short one-pager.
04:34 Kenji: For the Cloudward account where Anthropic is in play, can we co-demo cost-per-inference and latency comparisons?
04:41 Liam: Yes, we can produce side-by-side numbers and demo the Redwood runtime's batching and cache effects. It takes a bit of setup — we can reuse our benchmark harness — I'll add that to the action items.
04:54 Sofia: Also want a clear handoff doc — sequence of emails, who copies whom, and templates.
04:59 Maya: We'll draft outreach templates — partner intro, tech intro, and demo follow-up.
05:05 Marta: On the legal side, procurement wants to know indemnity and data residency language. Who handles that?
05:11 Maya: We'll send a short legal checklist; for any deviations we'll loop legal and start an NDA if needed.
05:18 Sofia: Good. On internal incentives — HyperEdge wants a referral credit or margin. Are you open to a structured referral rebate on closed ARR?
05:27 Maya: Yes, we can discuss referral credits for closed net-new logos; I'll include example splits in the one-pager.
05:34 Ravi: Cool. Anything else on the pipeline?
05:37 Kenji: One more technical note — some accounts will want model hosting options that support custom weights. Is Redwood able to host customer models?
05:45 Liam: We can host provided licensing is clear; we also support bringing-your-own-model for private deployments. We'll clarify model onboarding steps in the tech appendix.
05:56 Maya: Ok, recap. Action items: Maya to draft one-pager/pricing bands; Liam to share tech appendix & benchmark harness; HyperEdge to confirm top three logos and contacts. We'll aim to have those by next Thursday.
06:12 Ravi: Sounds good. Can we schedule a short internal co-sell kickoff with a 30-minute slot next week to get the AEs aligned?
06:19 Maya: Yes, I'll send a calendar invite.
06:22 Sofia: Also ask for an exec-level intro; that will help unblock procurement quickly.
06:27 Maya: Will do.
06:30 (crosstalk)
06:34 Elior: One operational ask — how are we tracking leads? Do you want to use a joint Salesforce campaign or have Redwood add to our pipeline?
06:44 Ravi: Let's do a joint Salesforce campaign so both sides can report. Marta will own the campaign setup.
06:51 Marta: Yep, I'll create the campaign and add people.
06:54 Maya: Perfect. Last Q — competitor positioning doc? We have a short note comparing Redwood to Vertex/Anthropic — will share.
07:04 Kenji: That will be helpful.
07:08 Maya: Ok thanks everyone. I'll circulate the one-pager and calendar invites; Liam will drop the tech appendix. Talk soon.
07:15 Meeting end.

Notes/Links referenced: co-sell spreadsheet (drive.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-example), draft partnership one-pager (will be attached), tech appendix & benchmark harness (internal link to repo).

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors (e.g., 'KeyV cash' for KV cache, 'Redwood Dedicate' for Redwood Dedicated). Speaker labels mostly accurate but some cross-talk at the end.
